references.text: Describes the building of the altar by the Jordan, which sparked conflict and concern among the other tribes
Continues the explanation of the altar's purpose—not for burnt offerings or sacrifices, but as a witness
The Mosaic law forbade offering sacrifices on any place, only at the place the Lord chose—this explains why the tribes had to explain the altar's purpose
The conclusion where the altar is given a name as a witness that the Lord is God—confirming that the altar was not for sacrifice
God's instruction regarding altar building and the purpose of burnt offerings and peace offerings—contrasting with this altar's non-sacrificial purpose
